hook: An HIV drug class strips envelope protein from new virus particles by triggering early protease activity
summary: Some HIV reverse transcriptase inhibitors also switch on the viral protease too early inside producer cells. Using the compound Pyr01, the authors showed that this lowers the envelope glycoprotein and enzymes packed into virions and loosens their membranes, cutting infectivity. The effect needs an active protease. The work is in cell culture, so its clinical value for these compounds remains open.
title: NON-NUCLEOSIDE REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE INHIBITORS BLOCK THE INCORPORATION OF VIRAL GLYCOPROTEINS INTO HIV-1 VIRIONS
